newsitem.title: USA: Barnes & Noble cut losses in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Barnes & Noble cut losses in first quarter.

text.p: Barnes & Noble Inc. Thursday reported a smaller loss than investors had expected for the first quarter, aided by strong sales growth at its large-format superstores and at stores open at least a year.
The company, which calls itself the world's largest bookseller, also said it was encouraged by early sales trends from its new Internet business.

Barnes & Noble went online with its own Web site last week as rival Amazon.com Inc., an online bookstore, went public. The two companies have clashed over the rights to the title of world's largest bookseller.
Barnes & Noble said its net loss narrowed to $3.9 million, or 12 cents a share, in the quarter ended on May 3, from a loss of $5.4 million, or 16 cents a share, a year earlier.

Wall Street analysts had forecast a loss of 15 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks estimates. Barnes & Noble stock rose 75 cents to $42.125 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Sales grew 17 percent to $596 million from $509 million while superstore revenues jumped 26 percent and sales at stores open at least a year rose 9 percent.

"We are also encouraged by early sales trends from our online business in America Online's Marketplace and our new World Wide Web site," Chairman Leonard Riggio said in a statement. "Since we launched this business, the number of online transactions has been increasing daily."
The company gave no other details about its business online.
The New York-based book retailer opened 16 Barnes & Noble stores in the quarter, bringing its total to 446 Barnes & Noble stores and 567 B. Dalton stores.
